questions_and_answers.question: In the sentence 'अगर न हो सके तो चिन्ता न कीजिये', what does the verb form 'हो सके' represent?

articles.text: Another verb form in Hindi is sometimes called the 'subjunctive' or 'contingent'. It resembles the future form but with the last syllable removed. This form has multiple meanings and is often used to ask advice or permission. For example, expressions like 'यहां बैठूं?' mean 'Shall I sit here?', and 'शुरू करें?' means 'Shall we start?'. With a different tone of voice, the same form can become a polite request or command, as in 'आप ज़रूर आयें, तब चलेंगे' ('You come; then we'll go'). The contingent form frequently appears in clauses beginning with 'अगर' (if) or in situations implying a possible or uncertain outcome. For instance, 'अगर आप चाहें तो आइये' (If you want to, come along), 'अगर आप कहें तो उनको बुला दूं' (If you say so, I'll call him), and 'अगर न हो सके तो चिन्ता न कीजिये' (If it can't be done, don't worry). In sentences with two clauses, the future tense may be used in the second clause for greater certainty, but the contingent is more common. The negative of this form is made by placing 'न' before the verb.
